<div id="requirements-class-openapi_3_0-clause">
<span id="toc42"></span>
<div id="_basic_requirements"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc43">10.1.  Basic requirements</h2><p id="_c9a3c3a0-dd92-d5f9-0354-084a6b86db9a">APIs conforming to this requirements class are documented as an <a href="https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/master/versions/3.0.0.md#oasDocument">OpenAPI Document</a>.</p>
<span id="rc_oas30"></span><!-- requirements-class -->
<span id="req_oas30_oas-definition-1"></span><!-- requirement: oas30/oas-definition-1 -->
<span id="req_oas30_oas-definition-2"></span><!-- requirement: oas30/oas-definition-2 -->
<span id="req_oas30_oas-impl"></span><!-- requirement: oas30/oas-impl --></div>
<div id="_complete_definition"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc44">10.2.  Complete definition</h2><span id="req_oas30_completeness"></span><!-- requirement: oas30/completeness -->
<p id="_a68191b2-1637-33ea-108d-7a0774cb71ae">Note that APIs that, for example, are access-controlled (see <a href="#security">Security</a>), support web cache validation, CORS or that use HTTP redirection will make use of additional HTTP status codes beyond regular codes such as <tt>200</tt> for successful GET requests and <tt>400</tt>, <tt>404</tt> or <tt>500</tt> for error situations. See <a href="#http_status_codes">Clause 7.5.1</a>.</p>
<p id="_7189e9f0-e0f6-f5e3-54e2-9fc41eef27ea">Clients have to be prepared to receive responses not documented in the OpenAPI definition. For example, additional errors may occur in the transport layer outside of the server.</p></div>
<div id="exceptions"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc45">10.3.  Exceptions</h2><span id="req_oas30_exceptions-codes"></span><!-- requirement: oas30/exceptions-codes -->
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Example  — An exception response object definition</p><div class="example" id="_b2cd9b6f-9781-2269-4f30-3742a9c88cf5"><pre class="prettyprint" id="_0b0624d4-dacc-568d-41b8-c8446a3b7cab">description: An error occurred.<br/>content:<br/>  application/json:<br/>    schema:<br/>      $ref: https://beta.schemas.opengis.net/ogcapi/common/part1/0.1/core/openapi/schemas/exception.yaml<br/>  text/html:<br/>    schema:<br/>      type: string</pre>
</div></div>
<div id="security"><h2 class="published-heading" id="toc46">10.4.  Security</h2><span id="req_oas30_security"></span><!-- requirement: oas30/security -->
<p id="_9798a402-7b76-a31c-69ab-c46e41e23a14">The OpenAPI specification currently supports the following <a href="https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/master/versions/3.0.0.md#security-scheme-object">security schemes</a>:</p>
<ul id="_c49411c4-653a-220f-fe79-cac523ca089b">
<li>
<p id="_f7d5435f-6081-e448-a77f-80189209f51b">HTTP authentication,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_f5baed9b-77fa-b638-9f62-be66af99378d">an API key (either as a header or as a query parameter),</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_ee021cb8-3c66-e73b-9ec2-54d5a77fa7e1">OAuth2’s common flows (implicit, password, application and access code) as defined in RFC6749, and</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_1badd91d-1fcc-98ee-d0be-bb1b7bca4f05">OpenID Connect Discovery.</p>
</li>
</ul></div>
</div>
